A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Evaluator Quality Baseline study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of the proxy baseline, including dataset-level results, proxy robustness checks, chain-of-thought experiments, and entropy analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds oracle-agreement measurements and alternative proxy-selection experiments in Appendices H and I.

M1.justification: The primary outcome-matching, proxy averaging, and preference-difference procedure remains unchanged. Appendix I introduces two tested procedural variants: retaining proxies with the same incorrect final answer, and retaining the two models closest in overall task accuracy.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same reported coverage: MATH500, MBPP-Plus, MMLU, AlpacaEval, TruthfulQA, German-English translation, CNN/DailyMail, XSUM, and QuALITY. The added agreement and proxy-selection checks reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 20 newly compares the all-proxy baseline against same-error and nearest-two-proxy strategies. Tables 12–15 also newly report specific reference comparisons, including AlpacaEval against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, absent from v1's reported AlpacaEval comparator list. The four reproduced prior-study pipelines remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.3 changes the reported summarization oracle from GPT 5.2 to GPT 5; this establishes a documentation-level protocol revision, not that experiments were rerun. Appendix I adds filtered-proxy evaluations aggregated across MATH500, MBPP-Plus, and MMLU.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds checks of agreement among the three DBG oracle judges and against their majority vote. Appendix I tests sensitivity to incorrect-answer matching and model-level capability matching. These extend the existing family-exclusion, proxy-count, chain-of-thought, and entropy analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly reports chance-corrected agreement estimates: pairwise kappa values of 0.603–0.678 and oracle-versus-majority values of 0.769–0.835. Existing paired t-tests and standard-error reporting remain; no additional seeds or repeated-run design is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1, Tables 9–11, and the relocated chain-of-thought table retain their numerical results. v4 adds detailed pairwise results for four retained evaluations and the agreement/filtering results. The entropy summary changes from 33/49 positive cases (67.3%) to 41/56 (73.2%), correcting aggregation while retaining the per-dataset sample counts.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the preference definitions, bias decomposition, outcome-matching condition, paired-test statistic, entropy expressions, and weighted proxy winrate. The added outcome-driven definition in Section 3.3 restates the existing preference differential; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The principal contribution and headline claims about the 89.6% baseline contribution and roughly half of findings retaining significance remain. Section 7 newly acknowledges that residual bias might arise from other experimental artifacts, qualifying its causal attribution to self-preference.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses different reasons for incorrect answers, stronger proxy pools, and sparse failures among capable judges. Section 6.2 expands the limitations of relative-quality matching and suggests rubric-based evaluation. New interpretations assert oracle agreement and proxy-strategy robustness, although Table 20 does not fully support the stated sign stability.

D1.justification: The v4 abstract newly states that this work's code and data are publicly available and supplies a repository link. v1 provides no corresponding access statement. Existing configuration tables and evaluator prompts are largely retained; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning relative to earlier self-preference, situational-awareness, and uncertainty studies remain unchanged. Changes such as Binder's publication year and the venue/year for Li's scoring-bias paper update the same works rather than introduce new references.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the abstract, adds focused explanatory and limitations paragraphs, introduces impact and acknowledgement sections, and moves the chain-of-thought appendix ahead of the prompts. Most main-section organization and prose remain closely matched to v1.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 moves to the opening page, main figures receive revised labels and legends, Table 1 is substantially resized, and appendix displays are redistributed. New pairwise-result, agreement, and proxy-comparison tables substantially extend the displays.

improvement.justification: The added oracle/proxy checks, fuller pairwise reporting, corrected entropy totals, code/data access statement, and more qualified conclusion modestly improve auditability and evidential support. The gains are limited: headline results remain unchanged, and Appendix I overstates stability—Table 20 shows four models changing sign across strategies despite the text saying two. The revision improves reporting without resolving the central limitations of proxy-based causal attribution.
